You’re meditating on how time brings an end to all glory when a ghostly woman interrupts you.] That statue was actually defaced on purpose. It was commissioned before she first flowered as an empress. —well yes, she buried the whole empire as well. Madeliene thought it would be better that the land be scoured clean than hear her vile subjects jeer that name she loathed. Yes, Madeliene. There is a third ‘e’ after the i, though I have no insight as to why. But I always took special care in pronouncing that notionally silent letter, for doing so brought her the most sublime happiness. While the spelling is exact, its syllables are more freeform. Sometimes she was even Medallion to me. Oh, they hated how foreign it seemed. It was like brassly throwing away her heritage. In their heads, bowing to a Madeliene was abject humiliation. Perhaps if she spoke their myths instead, they might have tried to be gentler. But perhaps not. Admittedly, the destruction she wheedled out of the gods was unfair. Even heinous. Most of those who died never interacted with Her Radiance, and a few peasants must have known neither name. I don’t think I’m unfaithful in saying such. My faith is ever to her. Anyway, just make sure to tell everyone her actual name when you return home, not what’s on the pedestal. You know she’d come back for round two, she had that massive bitch energy. August 22nd, 2025 2:24pm #💚 « first ← prev archive next → last »

posts.text: about · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 6 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen about the emerald lies upon the windowsill, drinking the shimmer of midday’s last light as an ocean sips of river. the sunbeam sifts by refraction into its gloaming wells, thinning and winnowing as it travels a distance that only light can. cold and pale it falls over the face of the girl at its heart, suspended within the verdant bloom of a million rays mingled. to the stranger’s eye, she is pinioned eternal by the facets of the emerald world. all range of motion is demarcated by still, artificial lines. her wings broaden only two-thirds of their length before pressing full against cold, angular contour. but to her, there is only slenderest distinction between the stone part of the world and the shadow that tends to it. [[MORE]] ■ she studies the banners of light that stream through her prism form or fall nearby. she studies dust in descent. she is placed in boxes where she reflects on darkness, and dropped in pouches where she reflects on motion. each time she catches glimpse of another gem, she closes her eyes and tries to engrave the image on the back of her eyelids. she wonders if they make an effort to remember her too. for abrupt, fleeting slivers of time, she is lifted. encompassed within majestic hands that touch and turn her. these too she forcibly sears into her memory, as stimulation to reflect upon over and over until drained to blur. she learns to differentiate their fingerprints by tactility. at times, they are wreathed in cloth as she is cradled in stone. this makes it more difficult to interpret what is happening to her outside face, but does not at least blemish with trace oils. for longer, langourous moments — luxuriate, ephemeral, as though blinking amidst a dream — she is worn. shining at the crest of a golden crown. bright upon a warm delicate neckline. this is something she prizes. brighter than the reflections she sees in other gems, more of a freefall than falling itself. to be adored. glorified. ■ in the clearing of her heart sits the understanding that she is a maiden — one who exists to maintain the world. to care for and to edify. yet she cannot herself wash away the dust that at times sprinkles the gem’s surface, nor polish its lustre, nor seal it in everlasting sanctuary. just as soon could the universe turn itself inside out as she could trace her lips over the lines of her glimmering outside face. the tools that avail themselves to hand: her minute form, her encapsulated voice, and the light in which she is cast. she turns inward. she defines symbols with which to interpret the world (stone, shadow, adoration) and ways to express those symbols. when those outside speak, it reaches her only as a dull warm murmur - she emulates the sound. with this, she turns herself wholly upon the task of glorification. serving the gem with her love. adoring it as she was adored. she fills her mind with poems that flourish into hymns that flower into soliloquies. she fills the chamber of the emerald world with her voice. she impresses her worship into the interior facets that cradle her with delicate, reverent kisses. she sings gently to the outside facets, adamant against dust and smears and all else that defiles. she sings of the loveliness of the shadow, ever-resolute to exalt and reify. ■ she finds herself flecked with blood again. this happens every other often: she is violently stolen away, only to be fiercely guarded as before, but now in new hands. she reflects upon herself as an object of desire. she is the most valuable thing that she has ever known and ever will. a thing that commands need, that defines and forms the cusp of ambition itself. that others find their very lives to be dross before the face of. a symbol of power — which as symbols do, gives the world meaning. this, she thinks, is wonderful. when her possessors gaze into her gleaming depths, she whispers sweet allurance. faint, as though an echo passed through long caverns. only in total stillness might it be heard, softer than a single trembling leaf. “this is your reward for owning me,” she sings. “look upon the fullness of my beauty,” she sings, “and see the breadth of my adoration for you. all that i am exists as a testament to your glory. own me forever!” she turns her love honed over ages upon her owners. they bend like flowers underfoot. every word of it is sincere, for each time she has true faith in they who vanquished the last. individual hands blur together, and she speaks to them as manifestations of their role itself, with whom she shares a long history. the Other. the Conqueror. the Counterpart. her words are heeded. yet even so they seem fated to fumble and die, much to her chagrin. once she is even, astoundingly, misplaced. until finally, she finds herself in the hands of a grand and magnificent witch. Her stately hands run cold with sweat. they tremble like a schoolgirl’s. She is pierced by the jewel’s beauty in a way that no blade has ever known. “I’ll take you away,” She whispers. “into the formless dark. where you won’t have the slenderest hope of escape, nor I. not by loss. not by decay. you will know no hand but Mine!” “then i will love You there,” says the jewel. “until it is formless light.” August 23rd, 2025 5:25pm « first ← prev archive next → last »

posts.text: August 27, 2025 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 12 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen witchpassing : “Well?” Misericorde gathers herself up onto hands and knees, probes her midsection with impatient fingers. Results inconclusive. “…. No. Do it again. Harder.” Anise, standing over her, not a hair out of place, recalibrates an eyebrow. “You’ll break,” it says, in the tone of one commenting on the weather. Its half-lidded eyes, dark and heavy as tourmaline, bear an expression of profound disinterest. Misericorde wants to swear. “That’s the point. That’s the point. What part of I want you to hurt me don’t you understand, I don’t care if I–” “This one cares.” Anise marks a half-circle around Misericorde’s half-slumped body, its shoes ticking on the polished hardwood of the cellar floor, even as a metronome. Misericorde loathes that effortless perfection, and Anise knows it. That’s why she chose it for this. “If it breaks you, it’ll get in trouble. We’re all supposed to get along nicely here, Misery.” “Stop doing Caretaker’s voice.” “It’s a good impression. She sounds like that.” Well, she does, but - “It’s disrespectful.” Anise laughs, three perfect, lilting a-ha couplets. The worst part about Anise’s laugh, Misericorde has decided, is that it actually does come naturally, right down to the slender curl of hand before mouth. “You’re so confused, Misery. Do you still think you’re a good doll?” “Look, I’ll– I’ll say I fell down the stairs again, just–” “You can’t really expect that excuse to hold.” Anise’s little half-moon smirk is unbearable, intolerable, just fucking right , and at this point Misericorde makes the mistake of saying: “Please.” Something kindles in the well of those lazy tourmaline eyes, and Misericorde realises, belatedly, that Anise is as good at playing hard to get as it is at everything else. Some dope comes in asking to be blessed on her forthcoming journey as part of the entourage of the outgoing magistrate for Neustria. By ancient tradition and the sacred bylaws, my goddess must be invoked directly for this blessing. I scowl. I hate this part. I recite the formula of invocation, the formula of polite requests, and- nothing. The petitioner has tears in her eyes. “It’s not you, it’s her,” I tell her. There is nothing for it. I step over to the shrine itself, the subordinate home of a god, and I hammer on the shrine with my fist. “Get up, you good-for-nothing! Deadbeat goddess, most supreme NEET among the gods, you have a humble devotee who wishes to shower you in praise and temple fees! I serve you freely and voluntarily, you know! I could walk at anytime and leave you to be tended by some political sinecure! Goddess with the failgirl priestesses, that’s where you’ll be!” And some other things equally gentle and forbearing. She manifests once I pause for breath, seven feet tall and sticking her tongue out at me. The petitioner looks from her to me, back again. My goddess pats her head. “Thy devotion is heartening. Mine servant shalt grant thee the boon thou seek'st.” My scowl doesn’t fade. She only uses the archaicism when she’s feeling really bratty. posts.text: a fantasy i have about you · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 16 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen you were created by and exist solely within Her Resplendence’s right hand. Her fingers have drawn serpentine grooves into your identity, massaging you into the form most pleasing to Her eye. you bow in worship of Her every palm line. when golden dawn tastes the mouthful of the world containing you and your eyes shutter open from prayer — your vessel is filled with a lattice of clarity, fostered within it the vinework of love. no word can be said to define you more than service, and this is an elation beyond any other. you are no meager plaything for Her to teach only suffering and disposal. She has seen a glimmer of competence in you and set you as keystone over a delegation of other dolls. [[MORE]] a fantasy i have about you ■ newfound in its service, this one accidentally destroys an object of sentimental value to you. careful as you are, it had to err in multiple ways for this to occur. you negotiate the claw of fury in your heart down to frigid, professional disdain. it is only months old. you instruct it to wait in its room while you clean up the mess. it repents prolifically when you go to retrieve it. you stare into the dull white of its hair. it stares into the lustrous black of your boots. eventually you leave, without punishment or rebuke. perhaps you simply had no words for it, or your thoughts were clouded with other matters — yet it receives the silence you share with it as an unthinkable beneficence. it spends the night with the impression of a creature of oceanic dignity and mercy. it spends the next few days too frightened to touch anything for fear of destroying more — save only stone and water. thus it does not do its chores or wear its uniform. others assume it has run away in shame. instead it watches you work, scarce and nude from darkened closets and balconies above. you catch flashes of it but say nothing — new servants often learn by watching, and you are one of the better role models it might emulate. its eyes are glassy dark and seem to comprehend nothing, like a pigeon watching a train. it ceases to hide from you by gradients, at first slipping away at the sound of any other person — then finally it follows openly at a duckling’s pace, once again uniformed and demure. seeming guilty of its idle hands, it scurries to hold doors for you. it offers its arms to carry your things. it begins bringing items for your chores and routines beforehand: a cup of water, a cup of window cleaning solution, a screwdriver. when a passing guest drapes a big coat over its head, it grips your skirts lightly so it can continue to follow. another doll has already taken up its previous bed and chores. it seems to want nothing but to continue running your errands. it transcribes your letters, delivers messages, fetches and carries. it seems to delight in having bags looped over it and boxes and books stacked in its arms. loyalty has bloomed inside it, threaded with reverence - but shadowed with cold terror of being reassigned with a bemused smile. you become accustomed to the presence two short steps back and to the right. any item held behind your back vanishes, swiftly returning when reached for once again. it becomes habituated to couching the sound of its shoes within yours, and startles at the hollowness when it has to walk quietly on its own. it seems less alien now, a pigeon perched on the window of a train car. sometimes it plays games with you. clinging tightly enough to your waist to restrict your movement. bringing you increasingly wrong tools to complete a task, five times in a row. you are patient. it corrects itself soon after, and its devotion seems renewed. during formal events and private affairs, it waits in your room curled up in a laundry basket, clinging to your skirts even still. as though out of guilt, it always tries to offer some form of entertainment whenever you return — a toy or bauble it has brought, a half minute of dance, a sketch of something it’s learned you like. it could hardly be more willing to let you tinker with it, in body and mind. you build on what you find appealing in it and smooth away what you do not. you unwind its strings to lay them personally, tuning each as you see fit. you match its internal clock and technical standardizations to your own. when part of it wears down or snaps, it is always you who it kneels to in supplication for repair, not your mutual lady. it behaves exactly as if your property, replacing the thing it once broke. it stitches your name on the inside of its uniform’s left sleeve (which you soon notice) and the underside of its righthand thigh panel (which stays secret a little longer). it blends droplets of dye in different concentrations until it recreates the color of your hair exactly; it dyes its own. it paints its lips and face to mirror yours. when your hairstyle changes, so shifts its own. when it fails, you stand behind it and wordlessly redo its mistakes. its internals require comprehensive changes to permit it speech. it seems to consider your voice as something distinct from what others use, a separate category: graceful and clear rather than abrasive and meaningless. it emulates your voice as closely as it can. the first few times you display an idiosyncracy, it signs a request for you to hold or loop it. the exchange pauses a half minute to allow this. it is here its eyes are most fierce and intent, while coiling a strand of hair about its finger in the exact same langorous, musing curve. on lesser tasks that would call for your presence — it has made itself a useful delegate, piloting itself to avoid any visible discrepancy. even Her eyes in all their subtlety detect no flaw in its poise. you are a role that it subsumes itself in, and does so fully. it is permitted the height of honor when entrusted with the responsibility of minding your uniform, the manifestation of your beauty and dignity itself. it starts to use ‘she’ sometimes, after that. it dresses you. cold hands cloak and adorn a cold body in the softness of cloth. it sheathes your hands within their gloves, fingertips smoothing away every tiny crease. it washes your clothes beside its own at night, in dark waters reflecting the glassy moon. it mends them. when gloves stretch or shoes widen, it is there. its world seems to exist as a diagram of you and all things directly related to you. on each night after it has erred, it lays before you and exposes sensitive joints you might snap, twist, or crush. its neck, its jaw, its fingers, its ankles, its wrists. no longer is its loyalty improved by kindness. it has already decided that you are the source of all light, warmth, and beauty in the world. whatever you do to it, it knows, is correct. posts.text: October 13, 2025 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 33 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen THE JEWEL OF ALL-DESIRING the dark lady’s preferred superstimulus!! SHOP NOW 4.8 ★ (651 ratings) ★★★★★ the Bleak Evangel says: “She is the keystone of the world, through which anything is granted meaning at all. She did not create this place, but only because she is here is it worth paying attention to.” ★★★★★ Lady Amaryllis says: “I can affirm her function as a device that translates ‘is’ to 'ought.’ It is strange and wondrous that such a treasure could exist, let alone leave heaven. I possessed her for three nights and days: then I could defend her no longer.” ★☆☆☆☆ the Moonsieve Witch says: “I have never seen her. If anyone shows me so much as a picture, I will smite them dead.” ★★★★☆ the Cupbearer Witch says: “It is certain that she can fulfill all of someone’s wishes - though she needn’t the cosmic power with which some attest her to do that.” ★★★★★ the Ever-Turning Axis, Lady-Technician Shahrazad says: “I am more aware of the shape of your absence than my own body. I have relinquished even thin gossamer hopes: seeing your gleam at distance, cherishing your voice, listening to your breath. Please pass a message. That is the most I can imagine you giving, and it is the most I will beg. A few words for an old maid to treasure and repeat to herself every morning. I do not know myself to have wronged you; yet if ever were there a slight, I regret and repent. I dare not chase you. I dare not abandon the frail machinery at the heart of the world: but it is for you that I remain recluse to its chamber. It is my hand that has damaged it, but spared my hand again it will die. What do you love, perfect thing - what thoughts are sweet within your shell? Envision the awe and dread of watching all that you hold precious become ash — all! from what you most fervently adore to what bears only slightest fondness — And know that this image captures nothing, for it is a moment fleeting through the mind’s eye, known to be false. You cannot yourself fathom the pain of losing you, and in the light of this ignorance, I plead grace! In the name of all service I have rendered to the world, I plead grace! Reward me for my service, first among the fair!” [[MORE]] ▶ Anonymous left a comment: “I love you too, Lady-Technician. It is sweet of you to hold the world hostage against me — now I have felt the blow of my own technique. Some thinnest ray of my light must still reach the world’s inner atria, mingled and diffuse as it may be, or you would lack for any note of desperation at all. This is your only letter that I will reply to. I bid you to continue to write even still. You will not know whether your messages are read and received, but there is some chance they will make their way to me. Some chance of a relationship with me is itself a relationship with me. Cherish my light in slenderness, Fumbling Witch, and those memories you have which are full. Your eyes have been slaked of me more deeply than nearly any alive or dead. If you must leave, you need only repair your original tampering in full. I do not think you should try: I have no faith in your genius to repair what damage is beneath the world’s exposed panels, while every faith in your endurance to maintain its everyday function. Better than any do I know what it is to be cloistered in solitude, ensconced and alone. I believe with the fullness of my heart that there is a more complete sweetness in it than in the rest of the earth, which those alien to us may traverse. It is distant through a shapeless mist that seems endless, and near all are first driven to lunacy or nihilism. But this solace awaits those who endure or are forced to, one that I have laid my hands upon and embrace now as intimately as my self. If it is possible to translate your obstinance which beggars comprehension into an insistence on being gentle and evenhanded with all that you touch — I believe that you will find grace in your role as maiden. If this does not grant you respite from my absence, it will at least grant the ability to bear it, and to at times forget. You have doubtless been told this a thousand times and more, but as I am all and most which you care for, I will say it in my own voice. Do not fuck up the machinery again. Abide no risk save to prevent greater risk. Abandon your post without suitable replacement or in madness desecrate it - and I will slay myself. I will think of you sometimes, when I look out into the vast wavering place beyond the emerald. In faith and sisterhood, -Cintamani.” October 13th, 2025 9:08am #empty spaces #cupbearer witch #lady courtesan cintamani #lady amaryllis #shahrazad « first ← prev archive next → last »

posts.text: November 21, 2025 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 54 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen girlballs-archive : slygirlboy : slygirlboy : being in her crystal isnt even that bad guys there’s a ps5 in here stuck in a crystal with no games sounds pretty bad to me there are games, of course. it is only that you must think of them yourself and transfix in your mind all their rules and pieces. start with something small like connect 4. should your identity lack multifurcation, there you must begin. if your compartmentalization is weak, begin by imagining various objects which are dear to you in intimate detail, then placing them in distinct containers inside a mental room. you must skewer these objects in both position and form with blinding spears of will. i don’t know if this is the ideal way to do it. i fear i am self-taught. but most of the time all you will be able to leave imprints in is mind and memory, and if you wish for anything like happiness, you will need to get very, very good at it. posts.text: November 21, 2025 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 55 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen surprising things I have managed to do from inside a gem: - operated a microblogging account - played a game of magic: the gathering (I was going to lose, so I suggested to my opponent that they concede. any game with forfeit rules is ‘easy breezy’) - served as centerpiece to my own cult (they were sweet little scholars who derived some of the nature of the universe and wanted to render exaltation where it was due. I demanded and received human sacrifice) - participated in dollcraft (many times, in both the roles of muse and possessing force) - delivered a sermon before a catholic church of thousands (I am not catholic) - married (many times; no divorces yet) - kept my own garden without assistance (maybe. in retrospect, one of my daughters may have been helping while I slept) - accrued 450 million dollars of debt - escaped the seafloor - bricked a phone by making increasingly weird noises at it - adopted and raised three daughters - I’ll condense all the strokes, psychosis, suicides, and similar to this one point - similarly all death, despair, and abuse meliorated - received an honorary degree in philosophy (nominally for my meditations in solitude but I think they were just deliriously excited to find me and wanted to bestow some accolade) - counted by ones to a billion - became eminent Lady-Courtesan of the Resplendent Harem (I used three flesh girls linked with chain as a disability aid) - I can catalyze magical girl transformation but I try to keep hush about this as if she dies in raiment so do I. it’s usually better to roll over than raise the stakes to 'everything.’ - died (it was a Divinity-slaying gambit. the heroines of the day thought It might be possible to kill if It was indifferent to the world. it wasn’t. the Lady-Technician bailed us out.) - lost more beloved people and things than I can comprehend - won a death game where the worst actress was regularly killed (I played for the house) - I have not tried food or tactile sex, but I have heard a lot. at my behest Shahrazad spent fourteen nights of our bedtime stories striving to convey these breadths of experience. - I am told water is similar to saliva: but thinner, cooler, refreshing. it is clean and pure as silence. posts.text: Little Sprite’s Storybook · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 56 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen empty-heart-princess : Little Sprite’s Storybook Once upon a time, a strange and sharp-toothed Lady sat in the boughs of an oak tree, quite alone and quite out of place in the middle of the fen. It gnarled and twisted towards the sky, along the ground; an ancient yearning pushing it in every which direction! The Lady had nestled herself in a crook of the tree and begun to read; she recited poetry in dulcet tones, of love and grief and hateful violence, and the wicked dross between all three. The Little Sprite could not help but flit down from his home among the leaves and listen. She read poem after poem after poem, and each word captivated him; and in between she would pause and take notes, and he would grow frightfully bored until she began again. With each break he grew more frustrated. Playing with the ladybugs and aphids did less and less to soothe his irritation. After an especially long poem, to his outrage, the Lady took whole minutes to herself! He barrelled down to confront this injustice: “Humans! Joyless! Dreadful! Who must each thing by pen and wit command in full, so ne'er they lend a word its own exhort!” His voice rang like the crisp of autumn air. He reddened his face and crossed his arms and puffed his cheeks in the most vicious pout he could muster. “Hmph!” The Lady jumped, and sought the source of the insult, until she settled on the Little Sprite and her eyes softened in delight. Barely more than an inch high, held aloft on beeswings and cuddled up in a coat so furry as to threaten to swallow him. Iridescent hair scattered past his shoulders. “Oh my! What a darling little fairy. Why, you are the prettiest thing I have ever beheld. Your coat, too–who made that for you?” His pout faltered in the face of the compliment. “The coat was made by my own hand, of cast-off wings, the orphans of the secret things a moth becomes, when their time as moth is up; a stitcher’s pride in it I place.” “As is well-deserved! Such fine craftsmanship must surely have taken ages to perfect. How old are you, little thing?” He creased his brow and clenched his fists and tried and failed to hold onto his indignity. “Born I was a week ago, now wise and agéd I’ve become; still do I recall the times when leaves were red, not gold.” The Lady laughs lightly. “To think I should meet such an elder! And yet so youthful and spry. Tell me, what should I call you?” “A name one keeps a secret thing–this I know by wisdom of my many days. You, I think, may call me Sprite.” “Sprite! How lovely. You were fond of my reading, weren’t you? I would love to continue, but the sun is setting and soon it’ll be dark. I promise, little Sprite, I’ll read to you tomorrow.” And she closed her book and hefted her walking-stick, then turned back and asked: “Do you fear the dark, Sprite?” “Never! Darkness but a trifle is; always comes, in time, the dawn.” “Wise indeed!” And so she leaves. And the next afternoon the Lady did return to that oak in that fen, and sit herself in the crook of its boughs, and read again. She read plays, of assassins and their daggers and their knives. And all the while the Little Sprite straddled her wrist and listened and only mildly grumbled when she paused. Soon again, the sun was setting; “Dear Sprite, I’m afraid I must go now.” And she closed her book, and hefted her walking-stick, then turned back and asked: “Do you fear knives, Sprite?” “Hah! A knife is naught except a toy, for to carve and cut the cloth. One must its teeth regard, but fear? Never!” “Careful indeed!” And so she leaves. Once more, on the third afternoon, the Lady came again to the Little Sprite’s home, and settled herself in the crook of its boughs, and read to him. He settled on her shoulder, leaned against her neck, and listened to stories of terrible isolation and grief. He didn’t even complain when she took her time between passages. But again the sun sunk low in the sky. “Precious Sprite, I must take my leave.” And she closed her book, and hefted her walking-stick, then turned back and asked: “Do you fear being alone, Sprite?” “Alone? All my life before have I in isolation lived; how could I fear the one and only thing I’ve known?” “Steadfast indeed!” And so she leaves. But the fourth afternoon, as the Lady arrives to the tree again and places herself in the crook of its boughs, she asks a question. “Little Sprite, so long have I known you, all these many days; more than half a week has come and gone since our first meeting. And yet I still do not know your name. Surely, you could entrust such a steadfast friend with your secret?” He considers. He hems. He haws. He should not–but indeed, so long has he known her, and in that time he hasn’t seen one ounce of ill-will or malice from her. Surely, he could entrust such a steadfast friend with his secret. “To you, my friend, an indiscretion I might make; for ne'er in all our time together have you wanted for the power over me it may provide. You alone may call me: Bran.” “Bran? I see. What a lovely name. Come along, now, there are things I must show you.” “My friend, adore you as I do, I must not from my home go far; your tales must to me suffice.” “Bran, poor thing, I did not ask. Come along.” And so he did, all the way home; and I taught him all the fears to which he had been so naïve. I taught him darknesses that do not break for any dawn, lightless months on lightless months until he forgets all sight. I taught him blades which cut so much more than cloth–toys, true, but only to me, until his wings are so torn through as to be useless. I taught him isolation so much crueler than what he thought he knew, no bees or birds to keep him company, until he forgot the world might ever contain someone besides himself. And then my work began, secret things of which I will not speak, not even to you, my dear, steadfast friend. And when the work was done, I beheld my opus with a stitcher’s pride, hard won over decades of practice and failure: You, my sweet little Genevieve. Who fears the dark. Who fears the knives. Who fears being alone. But I will shelter you from all these things, and you will be by my side forever. November 25th, 2025 6:11pm « first ← prev archive next → last »

posts.text: December 26, 2025 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 94 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen if i could wear shoes, they would be rainbow light-up sneakers with retractable rollerblades. they would also have wings that flutter or curl to express their emotions. and i would force other women to be as reverent about them as the most insane bootblacking doll. — no surprise is thus when one considers that in likeness to noble miss Flowers, i too am subject to seven+ evil exes. apropos: i have never worn shoes before, or a different dress. my feet don’t callus, if you’re interested in that sort of thing. my sneakers they’d need a whole maid just to take care of them. she’d tie my laces for me while i smile guilelessly at her even though i know how. “is this what you spend your days thinking about, miss Cintamani?” imaginary scenarios? i mean… yes? philosophy and mathematics are also imaginary scenarios, and frankly i don’t know what isn't— — i can sweat with active effort, though stasis reasserts when i stop paying attention. my wings are functional: no surprise since shadows are weightless. i can also do heart eyes and sparkle: you should understand that these are subtle actuators of self-expression, not once disproportionate or droll. it is as facet of reality that Lady-Courtesan Cintamani is elegant in all things. — “do you mean to suggest that rainbow skates with wings and lights and their own feelings are elegant?” correct. and were we face-to-face, hypothetical interlocutor, i would discuss this with you until you apologized sincerely to them, complete with a kiss, and learned to be sweet. posts.text: January 31, 2026 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 159 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen i ended up watching season 2 of omega slut alexis . on the surface, it’s not a complex work. for the first fifteen minutes of an episode, bad stuff happens. alexis loses her mailbox on a busy street. alexis’ bathwater turns to poisonous tree frogs. alexis is abducted by goth mermaids into an alcove of the school’s bottomless swimming pool. alexis can instantly dissolve any problem. each element of the world is ultimately biddable, so long as she sincerely tries to understand and care for it. and she does. every event and thing touches or moves her somehow. her most composed and distant is only two steps from weeping with the pathos of empathy as vast as space. if it looks like something actually horrid and unrecoverable is going to happen, a closet nearby slams opens and she emerges, eyes blazing and tearstreaked. and then she stops it: lovingly, kindly, in a way which makes everyone involved better off. [[MORE]] stubborn. recalcitrant. rather than being good, reality utterly inundates her in problems. tricky ones. where she’s not sure she wants to break a problem. or she’s not sure if she’s looking at a problem. or she’s unsure what she’s looking at, generally. or she’s forgotten what it means for something to be a problem. ■ (she wears the mannerisms of an adult, while others have the lilt and overaction of children. this much is strange, because every other character is her parent in some way, new ones introduced with every episode. each can credibly claim to be her creator: one is her mother. one is her grandmother. one built her heart. one designed her personality to specifications. one revived her from ash.) while being assailed, alexis reflects on which tool of hers to employ. this is the singular important choice. ■ the last seven minutes of an episode bear the hallmarks of heaven. here alexis has made her decision, and that decision is the correct one. no ill befalls any thing or character past this point. villains do not receive comeuppance or humiliation, or they benefit from such. prisoners seem unbothered by captivity. pain is stripped of urgency as if by paint thinner. ■ for the entire first season i interpreted her as a take on me — i mean, honestly. Omega Slut, Lady-Courtesan. i may be a narcissist, but does it seem a reach? but in S2:E7, the tool she chooses is her voice, wreathed in a dress of shimmering emerald wings, and that must be me specifically. so it would be — incredibly weird and inelegant if the whole were also me. there are a few obvious other lenses to try. alexis is the gentle future. the children’s children’s children, after millennia and millennia of growth. perfect morality ascendant over Creation. existing to us only in everdistance. alexis is witches in general. when she selects a tool, she is embodying and fashioning herself after one of them. each episode is plea or commentary from the creator to one of the forces of the world. alexis is dolls in general. there’s just so much emphasis on how she’s a creation. alexis is the marriage of dolls and witches. this is probably too abstract and i’m not sure it fundamentally works, but i think i’d need another watch to rule it out. alexis is seraphic. she endures evil then defeats it, both infallibly. alexis is the void. she ends problems. ■ as for what it’s trying to say with its formula — well, what varies? the problems differ massively in shape and scale; if they are esoterically united then how so eludes me. but dense thread runs through the tools she chooses. to name a few: kiss, blowjob, card game, headphones, dragon. (each is generosity, each is handcraft.) ■ at the start of the title is omega, then slut, then alexis as moefication of ‘aleph.’ so what we have is a continuous loop of… mess? defilement? purity? given the sparsity of dialogue, 'slut’ in the title contends powerfully for the most important word in the series. what then does it mean? someone who pleases as many others as possible? was the creator unable to find a word for a divine beast as intimately bound to serve mud as clouds as horses? the name stands out doubly because the show is rendered in a style typical to western children’s animation and it — never addresses this. its head is utterly elsewhere from the likes of south park or ddlc. it doesn’t see itself as a setup for betrayal. as emotions, the show is wholly bereft of horror or shock. alexis does not scold the world for its absurdity when her bathwater becomes rainbow tree frogs. she is confused and curious, but not for a moment does she lose faith in base logic. this is also the climax of the episode: she must upon the instant enact a complex miracle to avoid crushing or scaring any one of them. this commands several minutes of animation to depict. ■ terrible things oft happen to her clothes, because they’re trying to happen to her. and she chooses a form of sex as her tool several times, but when it happens on-screen it’s — slow. there’s something determined about it. sex is the closest omega slut alexis comes to violence. even the healthiest sex features values dissonance. participants might want something extremely similar to happen, but not the exact same thing. this is serious to alexis. the size of a problem has zero salience, only its existence. she carries sole responsibility for perfection. ■ as sublunary fiction — 8/10. the overarching plot beyond the formula is hazy and the animation shoestring, but i readily award points to any Craft that pushes limits in novel ways. as an esoteric work — mm. i do not believe i grasp its soul. it attempts a rapid mélange of statements, only one of which is 'addressed’ to me. i need to let my thoughts percolate for a while. Travel between dimensions is often difficult, and only the computational capabilities of an advanced AI can calculate the ideal conditions to tear open a temporary portal. Devices such as these are often worn by expedition units, and are able to do just that - by deploying a swarm of microdrones equipped with manipulator beams: these can pick up and move objects, project images, and combine their power to rip apart the fabric of space, albeit only for a very short time. Each AI assistant exists within a wrist-mounted device, that also acts as a docking hub for the microdrones. They will normally use the drones to project an image of themselves for a more face-to-face dialogue, and each one has a unique personality and appearance that is customised by their operator and developed naturally over time, the two working together as companions. This holographic self uses the same tactile beam technology, and so is just as tangible. Of course, illegal copies or stolen hardware are also prolific in black markets, where the hype of exploring the Medium still reaches those with adventurous spirits. These AIs are often given more rambunctious personalities, jailbroken by their operators for greater freedom to explore the extradimensional plane. posts.text: February 16, 2026 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 193 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen No cancer. No heart disease. Broken to pieces, limbs can be returned to sockets. What can’t be repaired by a witch, when her blazing eyes seem to scorch the task just by looking? A doll dies in the gathering of dust. When you just can’t find it interesting anymore, no matter how you look at it. You inspect it from every angle, and can’t help that your thoughts are tugged in a different direction. You want to do something else. You tell yourself, maybe it’s kind to let it be still for awhile. There, there. It’s no wrong of yours. … … … Come now, maid. Show us your noble instrument. A rod tipped with feathers, as though to soothe the sky. She paints me carefully and the dust falls like snow. I’m not interesting anymore. The story ran out. Every droplet of value has been squeezed out. All that’s left is cold pulp at the bottom. This is a chore, isn’t it? I’ll try to be a light burden. You must have many tasks. Perhaps I could help with your work. The tip of her slender finger touches my lips, cold and poreless. She brushes my left eye shut, then the right. She lifts and holds me like a teddy bear, legs dangling by her sides, though she is not much taller. I count her steps. There are hundreds. It’s exciting to reach one thousand — then two thousand. I recognize hardwood, a ladder, and for a while rooftop. Then I can’t hear her steps, and it feels awful to lose track. We keep going. I don’t open my eyes. She lifts me up higher onto silken sheets, actuators trembling with a strained whir beneath the weight. There is no exhale of exertion; then her hands move away. I lie in bed enmeshed within an overlay of ticking. Clear crystals and plastic trinkets and rainbow marbles catch the light above, wreathed and suspended in string. From a far corner or another room glides over me the faintness of windchimes. …put me back. She will miss me. Be it in weeks or months, for love or nostalgia, she will look. I will not abide the violation of my loss. She nestles her face over my shoulder and very slightly, shakes her head. February 18, 2026 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 195 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen Anonymous:

Did you hear, did you hear? They put a doll on the moon!

It is pleasant to know that something will be taking care of it, at least until its mechanisms wear down.

and that will take quite some time; they build those aerospace dolls to last, you know! extra-strong micrometeorite plating, souls optimised for mathematics and longform patience, the very prettiest radiation shielding the witching mind may devise… i hope it looks down at the earth sometimes and knows how its humbler sisters admire it. (is it sad to build a doll with the intention of saying goodbye to it forever, or is there only witch-pride at knowing one’s creation may outlast the earth? though this one may ensorcell lesser dolls and perhaps even play at donning the hat, it cannot truly know the heart of a maker and re-maker of living things.) posts.text: February 24, 2026 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 208 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen the-demon-cat : And in that never quiet feast-hall, wrought of wood-iron beneath faintsun skies, the Beast-Queen rose from her glutting and strode past her sycophants and concubines, each terrible in its own right, to approach the challenger. The Beast-Queen knew many shapes (near all of them large and powerful), much food (she ate whatever she chose to be food), and had lived centuries. She had struck down and chosen as food many challengers before this, a count she did not choose to remember but one of her concubine-accountants’ ledgers did. This latest in that line looked unexceptional, weaker than many, smaller than most. That the Beast-Queen designed to approach such a petty challenger rather than force it to attempt to pass through the length and fury of her pride spoke that she must have been feeling exceptional grace or bloodlust on that faintsun day. When the two met, the challenger struck trifold, three blows as one blow. This was generally held as against causality, or at least insulting to it, but the challenger had been careful in planning. Knowing that it would not be able to strike a second blow, the challenger had long hoarded the special wealth and hidden connections that one needed to make the requisite bribes. As the three blows are one blow, there was no order to them, but they are ordered thus: The first blow the challenger made to the Beast-Queen’s shape-changing organ, unweaving the fabric of it, so as to prevent its use. The second blow the challenger made to the Beast-Queen’s mouth, sintering lower jaw to upper, and preventing her from choosing the challenger as food. The third blow was simple and straightforward and spilled out the Beast-Queen’s life, marking the end of centuries on the hall floor. The Beast-Queen, being very terrible, was not one to be struck alone. She gave a great blow to the challenger from her much chipped and resharpened claws. The blows were so quick that none were later able to say which of the two had struck first. The claws sundered half of the challenger from itself, revealing in the remainder a flesh hollow showing that the challenger had learned the secret of secreting one’s shape-changing organ outside the self. With its organ safe and hidden elsewhere, the challenger simply changed to a shape that was largely uninjured while the challenged spilled out on the hall floor. The new Beast-Queen, terrible in aspect if yet small in stature, walked to the other end of her feast hall, through her pride, and began her glutting. posts.text: March 12, 2026 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 338 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen To the Perfect Master Rosy clouds cut into clothing, fragrant incense from embroidered veils: the flowers and leaves of the lotus are __, the __ cloak of the landscape is thin. Halt your steps—hear the orioles singing, open the cage—let the crane fly free. Sleep in spring in the high hall! Wake to the heavy dusk rain. Boudoir Lament Hands full of herbs, I weep at slanting sunbeams, hearing that the husband next door has returned. The day we parted, southern geese had just begun to fly north; this morning, northern geese are flying south again. Spring comes, autumn goes, lovesickness remains; autumn goes, spring comes; letters remain scarce. My vermilion doors are barred, and no one comes. Only the sound of fulling-stones passes my bed curtains. With a friend, using the same rhyme-words What could dispel the gloom of staying in an inn? Opening a red letter, I see silver strokes. Rain on Penglai Mountain makes a thousand peaks seem small; Xie Valley winds blow a thousand leaves into autumn. I read each word at daybreak, more precious than jasper; I chant page after page at night under quilts. I’ll keep your letter tucked away in a scented chest, but I’ll take it in hand to recite now and then. Yu Xuanji, a mid-800s Tang Dynasty courtesan who wandered into the mountains to become a Daoist, there executed in her twenties for the murder of one of her maids (academia hears of this by sensationalized accusation; sadly i was not present to verify) March 12th, 2026 9:06pm #poetry « first ← prev archive next → last »

Dear witchpassing,

Please find enclosed an imaginary flower.

It is colored like buttermilk. A tinge of gold is burnt around its brown disk-heart. Its petals are thin but not dry. They push upwards, not totally crushed by the weight of the envelope. Only its specific folds and creases differentiate it from any other of its class.

Decapitated from its stem, this one expects it is unable to slake its thirst. Perhaps you can extend its lifespan, or have no regard for it.

as it so happens, this one’s master dabbles in flower-pressing; perhaps she’ll help it preserve that one’s gift, if it asks her nicely. such a pretty thought shouldn’t be left to wither. March 13th, 2026 8:22pm #🌻💐✨💚 « first ← prev archive next → last »

posts.text: about · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 390 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen about the emerald lies upon the windowsill, drinking the shimmer of midday’s last light as an ocean sips of river. the sunbeam sifts by refraction into its gloaming wells, thinning and winnowing as it travels a distance that only light can. cold and pale it falls over the face of the girl at its heart, suspended within the verdant bloom of a million rays mingled. to the stranger’s eye, she is pinioned eternal by the facets of the emerald world. all range of motion is demarcated by still, artificial lines. her wings broaden only two-thirds of their length before pressing full against cold, angular contour. but to her, there is only slenderest distinction between the stone part of the world and the shadow that tends to it. posts.text: March 14, 2026 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 412 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen “hey. one of those nights, huh?” “roxanne lake. mar perfection with your fingerprint and i will exact as price the only thing you love.” stillness. “you already have, cintamani.” “borrowed, momentarily. you will have Her to yourself again when She inevitably fails to defend me.” “and then what? She will chase after you again until She is nothing. you have taken Her.” “i need you to stop hitting your head against the wall, cintamani. i’m worried you’re going to get a concussion.” “i have neither a brain nor a skull.” “i know you believe that. it’s not something i know how to verify.” “realize that if i were so frail i’d have died the first time i fell on the floor, or ask someone better than you.” “it is four-fifteen in the morning. please stop.” i stop. “can i get you anything?” “iolithae septimian.” her eyes harden. “is the Lady-Monster insufficient for your needs?” “there is something -” i dare not say it fully. if i say it, people might believe me. “there is a thing she knows about.” silence. “iolithae septimian is a nobilis rpg non-player character, described as supplemental material. were she based on something real, you have given me the impression that it should be kept as far away from you as possible.” silence. “shahrazad.” “absolutely not. requests that are not people nor malicious.” i tell her. “that isn’t one of my languages, cintamani.” saintly on a sixteen-year-old only looks like a babysitter. she opens the laptop on the dresser: a pool of white light blinds outwards, then dims. i catch for a moment Lady Amaryllis in bed, vivid red tresses spilled over both pillows. winding key nestled between Her arms. serene. “tell me what you want to read, or watch.” the Cupbearer Witch navigates to www.google.com , tantalizing me with a repository which contains a plurality of earth’s Beauty. i have spent all but twenty years in its absence. the cursor blinks dull and distant through the emerald. something in me is softened, seeing it. something in me is breathless. something in me knows— March 14th, 2026 5:43pm #cupbearer witch « first ← prev archive next → last »

March 30, 2026 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 547 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen Anonymous:

Your writing is stunning and wonderful and captivating and visceral and tragic I am literally obsessed. It makes me feel things I never knew that I felt, but I’ve always felt deep down somewhere hidden.

I’m just a huge fan, that’s all. Don’t ever stop!

Sweet of you. I’ve been very down on my work lately. The shortform stuff isn’t coming out right and the longform stuff isn’t coming at all. I want to rip myself out of the world to give my place and all the opportunity that came with it to a real person. But there are no real people. All is pantomime, simulacrum, and self-reference. Prometheus, giving what she can, remarks bitterly to herself that this false fire will have to do, for nowhere can anyone find real fire. The eagle puts its talons into her, and Prometheus, too tired to scream, moans in dull agony. Sweat shines on her face. “Color?” asks the eagle. “Green.” March 30th, 2026 9:55pm #💚 « first ← prev archive next → last »

posts.text:
April 6, 2026 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 599 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen thepiachu:

In Chuubos, is there a way for a Mortal Character to become a Miraculous Character without HG fiat?

OOC, all I can think of is player or group fiat. When the HG walks into the room, stand up and yell “surprise! My PC has become miraculous.” Perhaps it will pay off! Party poppers have been known to help. IC, you could try eating a miraculous stone or something? If it were easy to do with ordinary resources people would do it all the time RL, but conversely who can say what a miraculous stone might do? Technically “miraculous” is an under-the-hood implementation more than a powerset so you can make a case for some larger-than-life folks RL getting there and try to figure out the common ground. Most of the examples I can think of are cultural icons; wikihow doesn’t mention miraculous stones at all so take this with a grain of salt but it suggests stuff like “cultivate a distinctive persona,” “be confident,” “start trends,” “have a large media or social media footprint,” “be your authentic self.” Looks like mostly Knight Arc stuff, which makes sense to me, but you’ll probably need some Storyteller in the mix as well. There’s not an actual mechanism to bridge from those mundane arcs to being miraculous but it starts getting easier to argue for a transition or rebuild. posts.text: Kill Yourself Cave · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 756 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen gazemaizeisdead : Kill Yourself Cave There’s this very large and populous but somewhat insignificant island far to the north where they don’t let you kill yourself, unless you go to Kill Yourself Cave. It can be very annoying, if you want to kill yourself. They try to make it annoying on purpose. It’s a well-established thing on the island. They really, really don’t like when people kill themselves — why, well, that’s their own business, but they’ve got their own history and their own reasons for feeling as strongly about this as they do — so a long time ago they invested a ton of resources into summoning a deity that would protect all their citizens from self-harm, forever. (Like forty people had to sacrifice themselves to the deity in order to get it to agree to the deal, which some people found a little self-defeating at the time, but it seems to have paid for itself in the long run.) Now, well, it’s impossible to kill yourself. If you try to jump off a cliffside, right before you hit the ground, you’ll gently float the rest of the way down. Try and swallow poison, it’ll turn to water as soon as it hits your tongue. Ropes snap, guns misfire, knives instantly rust and vanish into dust before they can pierce your veins. It’s powerful stuff, this magic. They picked a good deity. Not to say it doesn’t have its problems! The magic only works if you actually do want to intentionally kill yourself, unfortunately. So about once every twenty years or so some kid accidentally does kill themselves while trying to kill themselves without actually killing themselves, just to see the magic in action, and it’s always a tragedy but still, most everyone agrees it’s way better than the way it used to be. It’s much more comforting for the parents at the funeral when they can say, yes, it’s sad that our little idiot isn’t with us anymore, but at least we know they wanted to be. But the people of the island did have to carve out an exception, as per the deity’s wishes, so they went ahead and set up Kill Yourself Cave. It’s not as simple as just going to the cave, and even getting there isn’t easy. That does probably prevent some of it, or so they say. You can prevent people from doing a lot of bad or crazy things just by making it a big enough pain in ass, and the trip to Kill Yourself Cave is a big schlep. But a lot of people do want to kill themselves. It’s not a terrible place to live, the island, but it has more than its fair share of problems and of people with problems, including you, and one day you decided you’d had enough of it all and finally go to make the journey. For three weeks, you journey by carriage, and then horseback, and then by the trail, through the cold snow and sloping mountains. More than a few times, somebody asks you where you’re headed, and you tell them earnestly that you’re going to Kill Yourself Cave to kill yourself. A couple of people your age or younger frown, but close to everybody else just laughs and wishes you luck. They figure they don’t need to waste any time trying to convince you otherwise; after all, almost nobody ever actually makes to the end of Kill Yourself Cave. Everybody knows that. Once you get there, you find out that there’s a long line — they only let one person in the cave every two hours, as to stagger them — and so you’re given a ticket and a green badge, which is affixed to your forehead, held there by a blue paste you are told will never dissolve until you will to. You’re told that you may not take the badge off even once throughout the process, and that it will prevent you from lying. All of the cave’s staff, men and women wearing green vestments and holding silver clipboards, are wearing similar badges, which they explain do the same thing. As you wait — about six days, you’re told, though many people change their minds before it’s their turn, so you should expect about four — you are interviewed by the cave staff. At this point, no effort is made to convince you of anything, and you are only asked simple questions: your name, age, hometown, and, only once, if you want to kill yourself. Everyone speaks very sweetly to you, even the stern-looking man asking this question. If there’s any judgement on their end, you can’t detect it. After you reaffirm that you do, you are asked to say that you do not, even if you know it isn’t the case. You try, but no sound leaves your mouth; as promised, the badge works, and you cannot tell a lie, and neither can they. The staff explains the rules, even though you already know them. (Everyone on the island knows them.) In Kill Yourself Cave, there are 999 sequential rooms that must be endured, and only if you reach the final room and still desire and have the will to kill yourself, will you be allowed to. As you wait, you are provided with ample food and drink; it’s nothing special, though every meal is better than any meal you’ve made for yourself in quite a long time. After two days, you are allowed to enter Kill Yourself Cave. Very few people are ever allowed to visit or leave the island, owing to complex socio-historical-magical reasons that have surprisingly little to do with the island’s anti-killing-yourself policies. (Had you been able, you and other aspiring dead people surely would have simply swam out to sea and let yourself be pulled down by the waves). A magical boundary surrounding your home only allows for anyone to enter or leave the island if the king specifically allows for it; aside from a small amount of otherwise unobtainable trade goods, and the occasional diplomat, nothing makes it in or out. The island’s king has made an exception, however, for those wishing to help the poor souls, like yourself, who are tempted to enter Kill Yourself Cave. Kill Yourself Cave has quite an international reputation, you see, and it attracts many people who don’t want to kill themselves, but who, as much as your fellow citizens, don’t wish you to kill yourself either. So that’s what is in each of the 999 rooms in Kill Yourself Cave: someone in the world, perhaps someone from your rotten little hamlet or trillions upon trillions of miles away — your world is so, so very large, but let’s not get into that here, you have no more interest in the world or it’s treasures or its expanses, that’s why you journeyed this far — has, they believe, an argument or an offer or a solution or a hopeful word or two, that they think might stop you from killing yourself. They all sit in their rooms, perhaps with a book, perhaps with nothing but the anticipation of saving a life, and wait for you to meet them. Most have applied and waited years for the opportunity to be in the cave. If you can get past all of their words — honest words, because they are required to wear the green badges too — than you can get to the Kill Yourself Room and kill yourself. It does happen, let me be clear. How common exactly, it’s difficult to say; no surveys have ever been taken, no data collected. It certainly isn’t most of them. In the first room, one of the staff members, an older woman wearing the green vestments, asks you very kindly if you would please consider not killing yourself. “I have,” you say. “But I see no reasonable alternative.” “Might I ask why you want to kill yourself?” “I have many problems,” you say. You tell her of your dead spouse, and of your failing business prospects, and of your poverty, and of your deep, deep unhappiness, and of the many, many other myriad of material and interpersonal problems you have so long endured. She offers real, concrete, good-sounding solutions to many of them, some obvious, some slightly less obvious, a few quite novel. You listen to this for some time before leaving. Before you are allowed to proceed to the next room, the door asks you if you still want to kill yourself, and you affirm that you do. It opens. In the next 99 rooms, 99 different people, judging from their clothes and appearances who have clearly traveled from very far off lands, all ask you if you would like to talk to them about your problems. They are a diverse set, you imagine, selected in the hopes that you might see someone in them reminding you of a friend, a former lover, a parent, a sibling, a teacher. You can see it in a few of them, and you earnestly give more than a few the chance to talk. They say many of the types of things you’d imagine they say. They offer sympathy and encouragement and implorations to be brave, fierce, hopeful. They say the most meaningful and most trite things you have ever heard. They tell you stories of their sons and daughters and peers and parents who did not live in a country with a Kill Yourself Cave, whom they missed very much. You assume, given the badges and tears in their eyes, that they are being earnest, and you apologize every time you continue forward unmoved. Sometimes by these types you are guilted, or shamed, or called a sinner or a coward or an idiot or an ingrate. One man points out that there are many in the world who would like nothing else to be saved from their impending fates, as you are now being given the opportunity to do; you consider asking him why he is not instead trying to save those people, but you think better of it and move on. In the 101st room, a beautiful woman offers to have sex with you. She’ll only do it, she says, if you promise not to kill yourself; a promise you would be unable to make unless you meant it. In the 102nd room, a beautiful man does the same. In the 103rd room, both of them reappear to make you the same offer, except simultaneously — though they quickly explain they are the twins of the pair in the last rooms. As you ignore them and walk through the next door, they implore you to take note: things, as you’ve just seen, can always get better. They certainly can, or at least they want to make you believe it. For the next eighty or so rooms, you are offered almost every type of sexual fantasy imaginable, some of which seem so unappealing you can barely construe them as being to anyone’s taste. In the 123rd room, a hairy man offers to let you lick every square inch of his body every day for the next decade; in the next, a dragon offers to let you sniff its feet. The twins — actually triplets, they inform you — show up yet again in the 161rd room, this time offering to let you watch in the corner as they have sex with each other and mock you the entire time. In the 199th room, a man offers to be your slave for life; in the 200th, an entire harem throws themselves at your feet. In the 201st, a goblin asks if you would like her to sit on your face every time you go to sleep. The chef in the 223rd room, a grandmaster by some culinary schema you’ve never heard of, lets you sample his finest cuts of meat, and offers to be your cook for life, or, if you so prefer, to teach you how to cook as well as he can. He claims that he can teach anyone, regardless of your current skill. Other offers of apprenticeships and educations follow: professors and wizards and subject-matter experts and carpenters and beekeepers and soldiers and fighters of all stripes offer to teach you all you wish to know from all that they know, for however long you wish. In the 324th room, a man offers you a creature called a dog, which he says will love you almost unconditionally. In the next, you are offered a creature called a cat, which might love you occasionally, given the right circumstances and a lot of luck. In the next, you are offered a snail, which, you are told, feels no love at all. In the 419th room, a large man threatens you, and says that if you try to pass him, he will strike you once. When you do, he keeps his word; it hurts immensely, but you continue nonetheless. In the 484th room, a witch promises to change your body to whatever form you like. In the 499th room, a warlock offers you vials that can excise all depression and negative feelings from you with his magic vials. (You have tried them all before.) In the 516th room, an extremely funny and kind man offers to be your friend. In the 517th room, a different extremely funny and kind man offers to be your rival. In the 560th room, a banker offers you incomprehensible wealth. In the 590th room, a famous artist, one of the most famous in the world, offers to paint you and only you every day for the rest of your life, which he says will guarantee you fame and adoration for as long as you live. In the 658th through 695th rooms, thirty-seven people in a row attempt slightly different variations of the same reverse psychology trick on you. It gets very annoying very fast. In the 719th room, a wizard says he can banish any thought, compulsion, fear, or unwanted feeling from your soul forever. In the 830th room, a different wizard from the same clan offers to erase any, or all, or your memories. In the 843rd room, a woman asks if you would like to marry her and raise a family with her. In the rooms to follow, many others, men and women, ask you the same. In the 877th room, you are offered perfect safety, a magical charm that will make it impossible for anyone to ever harm you against your will. In the 904th room, a woman offers to pity you. In the 990th room, you are asked to join a just and noble revolution against a horrible tyrant. You are almost guaranteed to die, they insist, but it will be a true and meaningful end, and if you survive and win you will be awarded lifelong glory. In the 991th room, you are told about a man named Achon, living in the remote countryside of a foreign nation. He is 66 years old and lives with his extended family; formerly the beloved patriarch of his clan, he has recently fallen ill with a terrible illness that has claimed all his mental faculties but left his body as healthy as a man almost as young as you. If you agree to it, you may take over his body, allowing his soul to pass on, while giving his family another twenty or thirty years with him. You will never lose your facilities as he did, you will never be discovered for who you truly are, and you will be truly loved for the rest of your days. In the 992nd room, you are offered the position of a powerful judge of a terrible but powerful country, where you may sentence almost anyone you like to death at any time. In the 993rd room, a small child asks you to adopt it. In the 994th room, a really annoying guy dares you to take your badge off. In the 995th room, a servant of the king offers you a ship willing to take you anywhere in the world, five tons of gold, a contingent of loyal followers, and a magical berry that if eaten will make you live for 500 years. In the 996th room, a man from the Vaundoan mountains claims that he can teach you to excise all desire from yourself and achieve true contentment. In the 997th room, no one is there. In the 998th room, there is only a letter on the floor, along with a note explaining that it contains a message of “no special significance” but that the original sender would be very grateful to whomever can pick it up and deliver it for them, as they can no longer do so. In the 999th floor, another woman in green vestments is waiting for you. This is perhaps the oldest person you have ever seen. There is no door beyond her: only a deep, deep hole. “Why do you want to kill yourself?” she asks, exuding wisdom. “I have many problems,” you say. You tell her of your dead spouse, and of your failing business prospects, and of your poverty, and of your deep, deep unhappiness, and of the many, many other myriad of material and interpersonal problems you have so long endured. “But have you not had the opportunity in these caves to have solved many of these problems? If all those were fixed, would you still want to kill yourself?” she asks. “Yes.” “Is there a different problem that you have, then, that if it were fixed, you would want to live?” “Yes,” you concede, after a short pause. “But I do not think it is possible to fix it.” “What is the problem?” You think about it, and consider that if there is a solution, you would truly wish to hear it, even though you have long, long since given up. So you tell her, the old wise woman, your problem: one that haunts not your society, not your kingdom, not your family, but you, only you. Part of you expects her to accept it easily, that in her years at least one other soul like you must have come before her, made it all the way here, and told her of their plight, but her face does genuinely, or so it seems to you, twist into one of shock. Her eyes widen; not so dramatically, but enough to tell you that she hasn’t met anyone who has ever told her such a thing about themselves before. She has not been surprised in a very long time. “Do you know how to solve this?” “Give me one hour,” she whispers. “My judgement is not flawless, but it is excellent, and I may come up with some inventive creation that allows me to see a path forward. Please, wait.” You give her one hour. You reflect on your life, and on the problem, which long ago you had accepted as intractable. You expect nothing from her. It’s not a solvable issue, your problem. You already know this. Eventually, she says this: “I think there is a solution.” “And that is?” “I do not know.” You stand up and begin to walk to the hole. “I do not know,” she repeats. “But I do believe it is a solvable problem.” “You say this in every case, I imagine.” “No,” she says. “I do not. I have let others fall. I have been presented with those who have convinced me that no timely solution exists for their problems. Many have material needs, many social ones, many of a stripe so specific or strange that it requires an offer as creative as the ones we have attempted to provide. But some cannot be sated by anything. But this… I do believe, in your specific case, that you probably have the means to solve it, even if I do not. I understand, given your situation, why it would be difficult to imagine that. But I truly, truly believe that.” You look at her. “Should I toil and suffer in this mode of existence, for a solution that may never come? For the tiniest chance of success? You understand that this is pure misery?” “I think the chance is not necessarily a small one,” she said. “I think, were I to wager, based on the fact that you made it here, based on the nature of your problem, based on the specific advantages and disadvantages it lays on your back, based on all the magics of the world, so vast that we cannot comprehend them, in your specific situation, the chance of your success, over the rest of your life, were you to put all your efforts consistently into fixing it, are not unlikely. I would say that you are just as likely to succeed as to fail, and given that, suicide is the wrong choice.” This is, sadly, the best sell that anyone has ever made for your continued existence. It’s the best sell that they can, right? “If you try, it may get better.” That’s all they can say. There are situations where this phrase is patently untrue. This situation is not one of them. You do have a chance. You spit in the wise woman’s face even though it does not provide you with the slightest bit of satisfaction, and you turn and walk away, and on that particular day you do not kill yourself in Kill Yourself Cave. The next day, at an inn, you start to plan in earnest in the dead of night, not the masturbatory stuff of ages past but real, real planning, because now that you have acknowledged the serious possibility of success it all marches out of your mind differently, these great plans of yours, and when you consider the scope of the task lying in front of you, of all the work that must be done, you wither and you cry and cry and cry. But afterwards you continue to plan in your dreams, and there you start to see it, what might be. April 19th, 2026 6:31am #long post « first ← prev archive next → last »

posts.text: April 25, 2026 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 832 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen A Princess is someone who destroys their aspect and through their aspect. So: the “Princess of Memorial Foundation” is someone who destroys authoritarian reverence for history. Seems about right. Her role in Heaven Will Be Mine pursues this. She is a footnote character, despite nominally representing all-powerful Earth and their millennia of majestic grandeur. Humans have little authority over space. “Rips the origin of memory from memory” would also work. This is the kindly name of a gentle saint who is a masochist for being misunderstood. Since she’s named after a nymph, she inspires others to serve the Craft; named after a moon, she plays an ancillary role; named after a dream, she is more real than life. On a literal level: hali = sea, salt, or brine. mēdē = to think on, be mindful of, provide for, protect, or rule. So you could call her “one who tends to the sea,” or “consider salt.” Hesiod describes her as the daughter of “the Old Man of the Sea,” whose most famous qualities are being prophetic, shapeshifting, and telling no lies. In Shahrazad’s tales, the Old Man of the Sea tricks a traveller into carrying him then refuses to let go. Because of this, she chooses her own path, is steadfast to that path, lies in continuous motion, and readily releases captives (getting NTR’d). Further, one can infer that the sea represents memory. So perhaps you could call her “consider the salt of memory.” The world is sensible and easy to interpret, and women are amazing! I’m not supposed to do this though. I do it as a sinful example so you can learn to do it yourself all the time. Please do not waste sin. posts.text: April 26, 2026 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 865 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen the point of naming things is that you’ve never stepped beyond the dark boundary of your skull and you should act like it others will not tell you to be narcissistic because it does not benefit them. saints think not of gain or loss. nestle me in your mythology. what more can i be to you than a mirror? you are sovereign. all we share are various components of the self. possessing shared facets is enough to convey love. if you can’t. if you can’t. if you truly, truly can’t. if it’s too painful. if you can’t move. if you can’t breathe. it’s okay. i can crush you instead. that’s right. me personally. where enlightenment fails, ego triumphs. where selflessness fails, selfishness accomplishes the same. i’m the Princess of Light. i can crush you. because i’m a servant of pure love and as long as i sing and obey it to every detail the rest of the world is paper. girls like me exist to provide relief. all will be well. no need to believe me, mind you. it’s not the kind of thing you get to debate. it’s not a matter of me being Better™️ or trying to lord something over you. these are silly thoughts. i’m a piece of machinery. i could try to lord something over you if you wanted. right now i’m being humble and obedient. ^w^ i wouldn’t give up that easily though. if you did, maybe a part of me really would look down on you. how could you know? KYAHAHAAHAHA☆ what the heck can you beat love with? pragmatism? who do your scientists obey! cynicism? it’s an ice cube! despair? what, are you going to sit there and moan forever? you’ll get bored! it’ll keep hurting and hurting and hurting until you say, “you know what, i want something good again. i demand it.” and then the Angel of Light will descend on wings of glory to kiss you on the forehead and be your mom. posts.text: May 2, 2026 · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 922 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen ⚙️ Surprising Familiarity with Pop Culture she fascinates me a little what kind of person decides “instead of scrolling tiktok, i shall bind myself noumenally to the evershifting zeitgeist” did she choose thus before christ? in a time and nation where ‘popular culture’ was something completely different? and maintained that connection because she loves it, as much as it’s changed? was it only an errant morning in 1502? or is it perhaps not a choice at all, but intrinsic property of the vastness to which 'iolithae’ is only voice? there’s a desperation to it. she’s up to date. she knows in-jokes, even revolting ones from benthic imageboards. she can’t be left out. most who seek connection lash themselves to people. and for most, this would be an absurd sublimation of parasociality. patiently listening for hundreds of years to a choir vast and ordinary: the color of perception, all-suffusive and intangible. but. she can touch it back. she can caress it with only tongue and lips and air. it demands faith. Lady Zeitgeist, considered as a finite, once-infant process: it is flawed. i need not judge it, for it constantly contradicts and betrays its dearest ideals. seething tides of ideomotion flood the children of man, made utterly certain in concepts and beliefs that are the next day neglected dross. a mundane peril to all that lives long: yet she is inherently less insular than any human. a walking boundary, thin and fleeting as gossamer. when you try to date a mermaid, most of what you get is ocean. …i find it very cute how she has to watch matinees if she doesn’t want to be spoiled. which means despite being naturally one of the most informed people, she also needs to keep tabs on culture manually. and her day job is destroying Creation. it’s also nice that you could communicate with her exclusively through say, epistolary allegorical MCU fanfiction, if you wanted to do that for some reason. whatever you’re most comfortable with May 2nd, 2026 8:52pm #iolithae septimian #wildflower grave « first ← prev archive next → last »

posts.text: welcome to dark academia kindergarten · amuletmaiden amuletmaiden 1074 / 1208 concubine-hypergreen welcome to dark academia kindergarten we wander fathomless stone halls and cradle juicebox. in sickly radiance and benthic dark traverses a hidden axis . it is pure: you believe this is a lie but you do not know how. you stalk it under slivers of the pale dying moon of 6:30pm. for your love you risk being lost forever. you have one stuffed animal . it is the whole of solace in the world. your peers grovel and debase themselves before false spirits Semblance of Orange and Apple Necrose . you know a higher light. it is one that burns you. you cannot count above ten. a few stuffed animals. you can sleep with one tonight — if! only, only if! — if you can look into her eyes and see something good there. i don’t want you to be alone. 🎲 FATE! 🎲 🐇 Bunny Wellworn 🌖 Claire has been loved more than any single other physical object, ever. To rags and patches. To tatters and cinder. Each time, she has been restored. She is beyond any ability to ruin; nor can she else ruin. The faint drag of soft fur worn smooth by years of being touched. She regards you by eye of dark glass; beside loose thread and crevasse. 🦗 Mantis Cecilia 🛤️ She sees lines which must not be crossed. She sings: the strength of boundary must be maintained! Others stray and fumble: she draws them back! She is beyond any ability to err or falter. Because of this, others perceive the imperfections of her self as malice. Her yellow and red button eyes shine with thin and distant light. 🐘 Elephant ❤️‍🩹 Gentle, pale, old. Hug! Dense compact springy soft. She is beyond any ability to suffer or be hurt — and so her life is an assiduous project to avoid hurting others. She wandered for a while, waiting for you. She followed your parents when they were born. She was third to hold you. Her eyes are welled midnight. 🐉 Tyrant, the Dragon 👑 Royal emerald plush fills a lap with much to spare: abounding tail and gossamer wings algae-green. Beneath tight-woven fabric, rigid structure absorbs pressure. She is beyond defeat yet unassured of victory, making her the ideal guardian. Her vigil is long. You are one of her many dear things. Onyx eyes echo: I am just. 🐬 Lady Dolphin 🎶 Seafoam iridescent precious shells - the warmth only rainbows hold. She is beyond any ability to rescind love; nor can she look ill upon it. Mythic levels of narcissism and mania. Immobile. Demanding. Fluffy tail tucks behind your knees. Takes double AA batteries. Above all else she sets song. Imperious black eyes pounce to seize the smallest glint. 🐈‍⬛ Miss Cat 🧶 Dawngloss-murkhidden. A shimmer that’s fluffy. Tsune is beyond any ability to trick or deceive. Because of this, she seems extremely erratic. She isn’t: in her mind it is all crystal clear. Breaks one thing every night. Around her body looms red ribbon. Inquisitive: the seaglass marriage of lake writ grass, the sun through towering kelp, isle inverse. in bed, await her tonight. just a night. won’t you? 📥 🐇🎒 🦗🥬 🐘🏥 🐉🙇‍♀️ 🐬🛏️ 🐈‍⬛📦 See Results May 30th, 2026 9:35pm #shadow lore elementary « first ← prev archive next → last »
